To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) group-based preference elicition can reduce the time required to bootstrap new users into a recommender system and (b) group-based preference eliciton can improve new user satisfaction with recommended items.

(a) users can provide more useful information to a recommender system in less time if they are asked to express preferences across groups rather than across items, and (b), in doing so, they are more satisfied with their resulting recommendations.

(1) users can more quickly and effectively bootstrap new user personalization by expressing preferences for groups of related items; (2) this approach can be implemented in a way that is compatible with any collaborative-filtering-based recommendation algorithm; and (3) this approach can improve the quality of the initial recommendation list for new users.
